title: The Norman Conquest 1066 (KS3 History)
subject: History
strapline: The year of three kings and the battle that changed England.
facts: In January 1066 King Edward the Confessor died with no clear heir, sparking a succession crisis.
Three main claimants: Harold Godwinson (crowned first), Harald Hardrada of Norway, and William, Duke of Normandy.
Harold defeated Hardrada at the Battle of Stamford Bridge in the north in September 1066.
He then marched south and fought William at the Battle of Hastings on 14 October 1066.
Harold was killed and William won; William was crowned King of England on Christmas Day 1066.
To control England, the Normans built castles (first motte-and-bailey) and redistributed land to Norman lords (feudal system).
The Domesday Book (1086) recorded who owned what, so William could tax the country.

quick_quiz.q: On what date was the Battle of Hastings?
Who won the Battle of Hastings?
What survey did William order in 1086?

teacher_tips: Use the three-claimants setup to teach cause and contingency.
The Bayeux Tapestry is a great primary source to interrogate.
Link castles and the feudal system to "how do you control a conquered land?".
